valuation_philosophy.model_type: NAV / wind-down scenario valuation (NOT a growth-FCF DCF)
valuation_philosophy.why_not_growth_dcf: Asset Plus is an externally managed (Centuria), debt-free (0% LVR) single-asset vehicle whose entire portfolio is the 6-8 Munroe Lane office building in Albany, Auckland (independently valued at $105.5m, 75.6% occupied, at Mar-2026). Management's explicit, board-articulated strategy is: complete lease-up, sell the building, and put an orderly wind-up to a shareholder vote. There is no acquisition pipeline, no reinvestment of proceeds, and no terminal growth in a going-concern sense. Revenue and shareholders' equity have both compounded NEGATIVELY over 3-5 years (revenue 5yr CAGR -14.0%, equity 5yr CAGR -7.3%, NTA/share -11.2% over the last 2 years alone) as the company has shed assets (Graham Street sold Nov-2024) and absorbed valuation write-downs. A perpetuity-growth Gordon terminal value would capitalize a shrinking, terminating cash flow stream in perpetuity - a definitional error. Instead this model discounts (a) interim distributable cash flow (AFFO-style, net of leasing incentives) paid as dividends during the remaining lease-up period, and (b) a single terminal distribution equal to net sale proceeds of Munroe Lane plus residual cash, less transaction and wind-up costs, at the point of liquidation.
valuation_philosophy.stock_based_compensation: Not applicable. Asset Plus is externally managed by Centuria with no employees; StockBasedComp is genuinely nil across the full history. No SBC adjustment is made to FCF/AFFO.
valuation_philosophy.why_entry_price_can_exceed_intrinsic_val: The base-case cost of equity (17.4%, see wacc_build) is ABOVE the 15% IRR hurdle used for entry pricing, because of the small-cap illiquidity, single-asset concentration, and external-manager-conflict premiums layered onto the CAPM base. When the discount rate an investor actually requires (17.4%) exceeds the 15% hurdle used to define 'entry price', the entry price will sit modestly ABOVE the CoE-discounted intrinsic value - an investor willing to accept only a 15% return can pay more than what a 17.4%-return investor would pay. This is the correct and expected relationship, not an error; it reflects that APL's fair required return for its risk profile is genuinely above a generic 15% hurdle.
key_judgment_calls: Sale price scenarios are expressed as a percentage of the Mar-2026 independent valuation ($105.5m) rather than a DCF-derived value, because Bayleys' independent valuation already embeds a cap-rate/discount-rate view of the asset's cash flows; re-deriving that from scratch inside this model would double-count valuer judgment.

Interim AFFO paths are hand-built per scenario from FY2026 actuals ($169k AFFO after $3.01m leasing incentives; passing net rent $5.2m vs fully-leased $7.1-7.2m) and are assumed to decline in leasing-incentive drag as vacancy (currently 24.4%) fills.

Wind-up/transaction costs = ~1.5% of sale price (agency + legal, typical NZ commercial property transaction cost) plus a fixed $350-500k allowance for final audit, shareholder meeting, and deregistration costs.
No terminal growth rate or exit multiple is used - the terminal value IS the property sale proceeds net of costs, which is a liquidation value, not a going-concern capitalization.

inputs.sbc_source: not applicable - externally managed, no employees, zero SBC across full history
inputs.units: thousands (except shares_outstanding in thousands, nta_per_share and current_price in dollars/share)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: not applicable - wind-down vehicle, no growth rate is projected; historical CAGRs shown for context only and are uniformly negative, confirming this is a shrinking/liquidating entity rather than a compounder
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: N/A - model does not use a growth-CAGR-based FCF projection
historical_growth.notes: Revenue, shareholders' equity, and NTA/share have all declined over the trailing 3-5 years as the company sold Graham Street (Nov-2024), repaid all debt, and absorbed three consecutive years of unrealised property revaluation losses ($4.90m FY24, $7.16m FY25, $7.43m FY26). This is consistent with, and expected of, a single-asset wind-down vehicle and is not itself a red flag distinct from the wind-down thesis.

wacc_build.rationale: APL carries zero debt (0% LVR), so cost of equity = discount rate; no WACC blend is needed. CAPM base uses NZ 10yr govt bond yield (~4.75%) and NZ equity market ERP (~5.5%) with a below-1.0 beta (0.85) reflecting the low-leverage balance sheet, offset by four company-specific premiums: (1) small-cap illiquidity - APL trades a thin NZX micro-cap free float; (2) single-asset concentration - 100% of the portfolio is one Auckland office building with no diversification; (3) external-manager conflict - Centuria is both manager (fee-earner) and ~20% shareholder, with a board nominee no longer classified as independent from Oct-2025; (4) Albany office market risk - the North Shore office submarket vacancy rose from 9.5% to 11.7% over H2 2025, a structurally soft leasing market. Bull case reduces the discount rate 1.5pp (faster resolution, less uncertainty); bear case adds 2.0pp (prolonged wind-up, deeper distress).

base.scenario_narrative: Munroe Lane completes lease-up over ~2-3 years as MILK Orthodontics commences and remaining Levels 1/2 fill gradually; property sells at 95% of the Mar-2026 independent valuation ($105.5m) reflecting continued but not severe Albany office softness plus normal transaction friction; wind-up completes within ~3 years of this valuation date (by ~FY2029).

bull.scenario_narrative: Albany office vacancy recovers faster than expected; Munroe Lane reaches close to full occupancy within ~18-24 months on the back of MILK Orthodontics plus 1-2 further large leases; property sells at a premium to the independent valuation (103% of book) reflecting a fully-let, well-specified (5 Star Green Star) asset; wind-up completes within 2 years.

bear.scenario_narrative: Albany/North Shore office market softness persists or worsens (vacancy keeps climbing beyond 11.7%); lease-up of the remaining ~3,552m2 stalls, requiring further incentives; dividends are suspended to preserve cash for leasing capex and corporate overhead; the property eventually sells at a material discount to book (22% below the Mar-2026 valuation) after a prolonged ~5-year process, with cash eroded by ongoing vacancy carry and admin costs in the interim.

bear.note: Dividends suspended in bear case - all interim cash effects (burn and partial recovery) accrue to the terminal distribution rather than being paid out; no separate interim PV of dividends applies.

base.note_on_relationship_to_iv: Entry price is calculated on the BASE-case cash flow path (interim AFFO + terminal distribution) discounted at the 15% hurdle rate rather than the base-case cost of equity (17.43%). Because CoE (17.43%) exceeds the 15% hurdle, entry price is HIGHER than the CoE-discounted intrinsic value here - an investor targeting only a 15% return can justify paying more than the risk-adjusted fair value. This is the correct and expected mathematical relationship, not an anomaly (see valuation_philosophy).

sensitivity.axes: Rows = Cost of Equity (%), Columns = Sale price as % of Mar-2026 independent valuation ($105.5m). Base case = CoE 17.4%, sale 95% of book, cell = $0.190.

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Base case (management's stated plan proceeding roughly as guided) is given the largest weight as the modal outcome. Bear case is weighted above bull (30% vs 20%) because the near-term evidence - three consecutive years of NTA decline, a soft and worsening Albany office vacancy trend (9.5% to 11.7% in H2 2025), and AFFO of only $0.17m after incentive costs in FY2026 - skews the near-term risk distribution toward further delay/discount rather than an upside surprise. Bull case requires a faster-than-observed leasing recovery that has not yet shown up in the data.

cross_checks.note: Current price of $0.165 represents a ~46% discount to the Mar-2026 reported NTA of $0.307/share. The base-case wind-down IV of $0.190 (a 38% discount to NTA) reflects that even a successful, on-plan lease-up-and-sale outcome does not fully realize book value once transaction costs, further leasing incentive cash burn, and a 3-year discounting period are applied. The market price sits below even the bear-case IV of $0.0985 is false - current price ($0.165) actually sits ABOVE bear IV ($0.0985) and BELOW base IV ($0.190), i.e. within the base/bear range, consistent with the market pricing in meaningful execution and market risk but not the full bear scenario.

sanity_check.basis_note: Asset Plus has nil SBC (externally managed, no employees), so SBC-adjusted and unadjusted multiples are identical. Net income is negative in FY2024-FY2026 (unrealised property revaluation losses) so P/E is unavailable; EBITDA is not reported (IAS 40 property vehicle) so EV/EBITDA is unavailable. P/B is the meaningful multiple for a NAV/wind-down valuation and is computed from March-end monthly closes against FY shareholders' equity. These figures will not match screener P/B which uses live intraday data.

checks.implied_pb_vs_1.5x_hist_max: PASS - base implied P/B 0.62x (bull 0.79x) vs threshold 1.29x (1.5 x 10yr max 0.86x); even the bull case sits inside the historical trading range
checks.upside_gt_100_and_price_upper_half: PASS - base upside 15.2% and current price $0.165 is at the BOTTOM of the 10yr range ($0.163-$0.70)

sanity_check.diagnosis: No fix required. The base-case IV of $0.190 is itself a 38% discount to NTA ($0.307), the model already discounts a terminating cash-flow stream at a 17.4% cost of equity with four explicit structural risk premiums, and every scenario's implied P/B lies within the 10-year historical trading band (0.57x-0.86x).
